source.title: Deep Double Descent via Smooth Interpolation
source.authors: Matteo Gamba; Erik Englesson; Mårten Björkman; Hossein Azizpour

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures interpolation and test performance under label corruption, using input-space loss sharpness rather than the original studies’ fitting measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for CIFAR-10 with 20% noisy labels and for ResNets trained with all labels corrupted. It also reports other smoothness results, but those do not directly measure the claim versions. Results cited from prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports training-set interpolation and chance-level test performance with all CIFAR-10 labels corrupted, using the fitting measures named in V1. Its additional smoothness measures do not change that relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors' central conclusion is that overparameterization promotes smooth input-space interpolation of both clean and noisy training data. This smoothness can coexist with chance-level generalization when all training labels are corrupted.
record.recipe_differences: Uses deep networks trained on corrupted image labels, but studies input-space loss smoothness and test error rather than directly reproducing the original fitting measurements. The all-labels-corrupted result does not state the corruption procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Model width and training epoch affect interpolation and test error; the ResNet setup uses Adam, data augmentation and batch normalization, while the ConvNet setup uses SGD and no weight decay.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed 20% label corruption, test error follows double descent as model width increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test error can peak near the interpolation threshold and improve with further overparameterization.

fits_no_version.finding: Overparameterization promotes smooth interpolation around noisy training points, including when all labels are corrupted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-space smoothness around memorized noisy labels can increase without improving generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Small models predominantly fit clean labels and have close-to-zero accuracy on corrupted labels at convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Limited model capacity favors fitting clean patterns over corrupted labels; this comparison across widths does not establish temporal learning order.

record.problems: The all-corrupted-label experiment does not specify the corruption procedure or provide numerical results in the text. Some results are presented only in figures. The paper reports standard deviations over 3 seeds for Figure 2, but uncertainty for the all-corrupted result is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were identified for the other versions. Smoothness metrics and cited prior-work findings were left out because they do not directly measure those versions.

untested.parts: Independent random assignment of every training label is not documented. A matched true-label CIFAR-10 comparison establishing unchanged architecture and hyperparameters is not reported.
Relative convergence time for true versus random labels and slowing across increasing corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption-fraction sweep demonstrating perfect fitting throughout and steadily increasing test error toward chance. The 20% experiment establishes only a single-fraction fitting result.

Whether weight decay or dropout prevents fitting random labels, and whether removing explicit regularization preserves good true-label generalization. The all-corrupted ResNet setting supplies evidence only for fitting despite training augmentation.

An established temporal ordering of fitting real and noisy labels. Separate loss heatmaps are supplied, but their trajectories cannot be read from the provided text; the prose observation about small models concerns model size rather than learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The 20% corruption setting is not a scope failure of V1. No challenge follows from its test error being better than chance. The supplied text also inconsistently describes ResNet batch normalization, so its presence should not be treated as settled.

versions.untested_parts: The all-corrupted-label experiment does not specify how labels were corrupted or establish that each label was independently randomized. It does not report unchanged hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
The paper does not sweep corruption fractions from none to all and report steady test-error degradation across them.
The paper does not test whether explicit regularization prevents fitting random labels or whether its removal harms true-label generalization.
The paper does not measure the order in which real and noisy labels are learned.
